Neal Pionk had 12 points in 51 games for Winnipeg last season. He has 13 in 21 this year, playing more than 24 minutes a night for a Jets team that has won six straight. For an undrafted defenseman who has spent more than 500 games in Winnipeg, it is a timely rebound.

The odd part is that the luck has run against him. Teammates have scored 6.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and that kind of shortfall usually swings back. His own shooting is a little hot, and his scoring rate is above our talent range for him, so the two pull in opposite directions. He is getting pucks to the net, with 50 shots in 21 games.

At five-on-five, Winnipeg takes about 55% of the shot attempts with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season while facing top competition (92nd percentile), with chances against piling up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking is kinder: 65% of his exits keep the puck, and he was in the 81st percentile among defensemen for setting up teammates' shots.
headline: Neal Pionk is producing through some bad luck
